transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because for a really long time now, I just wake up already feeling low. It's like... there’s this heavy, gray feeling on me before I even get to the clinic for work, and it pretty much just follows me through the whole day.
How long has this heavy, gray feeling been happening? Has it been going on continuously, or does it come and go?

It's pretty much continuous. Um, I'd say it's been going on for about two years and two months now. It started right around the time the staffing changed at the clinic and my schedule started rotating all over the place. Since then, it just... hasn't really let up.

During these past two years and two months, have there been any stretches of time—maybe days or weeks—when you felt back to your normal self, or has the heavy, gray feeling been there pretty much every single day?

Um... no, not really. I haven't noticed any stretches like that. It's just... it's there pretty much every single day. I really can't remember a time in the last couple of years where I felt like my old self for a few days, let alone a whole week. It just stays with me.
During these two years and two months, have there been any periods—even just a month or two—where the heavy feeling completely went away and you felt fine?
No, honestly, there hasn't been a time like that. Not even for a month. It's just... it's just always there. I haven't had any break from it at all since it started.
Before these past two years and two months, did you ever have periods where you felt depressed or low like this—separate episodes that eventually got better on their own?
No, not really. Before this started a couple of years ago, I felt fine. I mean, I had normal bad days like anyone else, but nothing like this heavy feeling. It never got stuck like this before.

During these past two years, have there been any times when you felt unusually energetic, optimistic, or 'up'—maybe needing less sleep than usual, or feeling like you could do a lot of things at once?

No, definitely not. I haven't had any bursts of energy or felt unusually happy or anything. I always feel tired, so I definitely haven't felt like I needed less sleep. It's just been this constant low energy the whole time.

During these two years, have there been any times—even just a few days—when your mind felt like it was racing or you had a lot of thoughts coming quickly, or when you felt unusually productive or driven to do things, even if you didn't feel happy?

No, I haven't had anything like that. My mind doesn't really race... if anything, it feels like my thoughts are just slow. And I definitely haven't felt productive or driven to do much of anything. It's always a struggle just to get basic things done, so... no, no days like you're describing.

During these past two years, have you been able to enjoy things that you used to enjoy before—like hobbies, time with friends, or activities you found fun—or does everything feel kind of flat and uninteresting to you?

No, I haven't really been able to enjoy much of anything. It all just feels pretty flat, like you said. The stuff I used to think was fun just... doesn't interest me now. I don't really get any enjoyment out of hobbies or hanging out with people anymore. It just feels like going through the motions.
Have there been any stretches of time—maybe a week or longer—where you felt noticeably better, more confident, or more motivated than your usual baseline, even if you wouldn't call it 'happy'?
No, I haven't. There really haven't been any times where I felt better or more motivated. It's just been the same low feeling the whole time. I don't really have weeks where things feel easier.
During these two years, have there been any times when you felt particularly irritable, angry, or on edge—even if you wouldn't say you felt 'up' or energetic?

No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated sometimes just because everything is so hard to do, but... I wouldn't say I've had times where I felt unusually angry or on edge. It's more just a constant exhaustion. I don't really have the energy to get worked up or irritable like that.

Have there ever been any stretches of time, even just 4 or 5 days in a row, where you needed significantly less sleep than usual—like feeling rested after only 3 or 4 hours of sleep—and during those same days you were also able to get a lot more done than you normally do?

No, definitely not. I've never had a time where I could just sleep for three or four hours and feel fine. If anything, it's the opposite... I sleep a lot and still feel tired. I've never had a few days where I suddenly had all this energy to get things done. It's always just a struggle to do the bare minimum.

F45.9 and F48.9 (somatization and other neurotic disorders) included as differential for persistent somatic-emotional complaints, though less likely given clear mood description.
